messages.author: 249ba2bf0beed132
messages.subject: Troubling installing on Debian
parts:
I am having difficulty installing nimble on debian. I can install and build Rcpp and RcppArmadillo packages but for some reason, I get the following warning when installing nimble either from CRAN, from a tarball, or using devtools and installing from gitHub:

 

* installing *source* package ‘nimble’ ...
** package ‘nimble’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
checking whether the C++ compiler works... no
configure: error: in `/tmp/RtmpYpKAn9/R.INSTALL6b6f6a61b617/nimble':
configure: error: C++ compiler cannot create executables
See `config.log' for more details
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘nimble’
* removing ‘/home/jtipton/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.3/nimble’

The downloaded source packages are in
        ‘/tmp/RtmpLnFf6X/downloaded_packages’
Warning message:
In install.packages("nimble") :
  installation of package ‘nimble’ had non-zero exit status




I'm getting a warning saying the C++ compiler isn't compatible. The current compilers I have installed are


gcc --version

gcc (Debian 6.3.0-18+deb9u1) 6.3.0 20170516
Copyright (C) 2016 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.


gfortran --version

GNU Fortran (Debian 6.3.0-18+deb9u1) 6.3.0 20170516
Copyright (C) 2016 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.


g++ --version

g++ (Debian 6.3.0-18+deb9u1) 6.3.0 20170516
Copyright (C) 2016 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.


Thanks for any potential help.


John

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Troubling installing on Debian
parts:
Hi John,

Rather than trying to dig too deeply right away, I'm thinking it might
be worth having you upgrade R and see what happens. It looks like
you are on R 3.3, which is quite old. Can you upgrade to R 3.5.x or
3.6.x and see what happens?

If that doesn't work, can you include what is in config.log when you respond?

chris

John
